name: Tonic Warehouse LiDAR Cuboids
description: Annotation guidelines for 3D cuboids (bounding boxes) in warehouse LiDAR point clouds: 22 object classes in dynamic and static groups, occlusion and motion states, human activity states, persistent track IDs, pre-label review and 2D image alignment.

roi.requirement: good but optional if lidar points are bad

classes.name: Human
classes.definition: A person present in the scene, in any posture or activity (Standing, Walking, Running, Sitting, Kneeling, Bending, In-Wheelchair/ADA, etc.). Cuboid covers the full expected body volume, including any occluded portion.
cuboidRules: Cuboid shall encompass the expected physical body volume including head, torso, arms and legs
For partially occluded humans, estimate the hidden body portion and maintain a physically representative cuboid
Cuboids shall not be reduced solely to fit visible pixels

classes.name: Humanoid Robot
classes.definition: A bipedal, human-shaped robot performing tasks in the facility (e.g. picking, walking). Not a person - a robot built with a human-like body plan.
cuboidRules: For articulated poses, the cuboid shall represent the overall occupied space of the robot

images.caption: Humanoid robot standing in a lab, bipedal human-shaped body

classes.name: Forklift
classes.definition: A powered industrial truck with a fork/mast assembly used to lift and move palletized loads. Cuboid includes chassis, operator compartment, and forks.
cuboidRules: Cuboid shall encompass chassis, operator compartment and integrated fork assembly

images.caption: Yellow forklift with mast, operator compartment and forks

classes.name: Pallet Jack
classes.definition: A low-profile manual or powered truck with two forks that slide under a pallet to lift and move it short distances. Lower and smaller than a forklift; no raised mast.
cuboidRules: Cuboid shall encompass the pallet footprint
Cuboid shall encompass attached load when permanently associated with the pallet

images.caption: Yellow manual pallet jack with two forks and a handle

classes.name: Cart
classes.definition: A wheeled, hand-pushed or hand-pulled cart used to carry goods, tools, or totes (e.g. a push cart or hand truck). Not motorized and not a pallet jack.

images.caption: Black two-tier utility push cart
Red flat-bed platform cart with push handle

classes.name: AGV / AMR
classes.definition: An Automated Guided Vehicle or Autonomous Mobile Robot: a driverless, self-navigating robotic vehicle that moves goods without an onboard human operator.

images.caption: Side-by-side comparison of an AMR (left) and an AGV (right)

classes.name: Wheelchair
classes.definition: A wheeled mobility device. Annotate the device itself with this class; if a person is using it, also annotate the person as Human with activity state In-Wheelchair/ADA.
cuboidRules: If occupied, annotate BOTH the wheelchair (Wheelchair) and the person (Human, activity In-Wheelchair/ADA)

images.caption: Empty manual wheelchair

classes.name: Vehicle
classes.definition: Any motorized vehicle which doesn't belong to the other mentioned category.

images.caption: Car body frames on an assembly line with orange robot arms (Vehicle example)

classes.name: Pallet
classes.definition: A flat wooden or plastic transport structure used as a base for stacking goods. Cuboid covers the pallet footprint plus any load permanently attached to it.
cuboidRules: Cuboid covers pallet footprint plus any load permanently attached to it

images.caption: Stacks of empty wooden pallets

classes.name: Tote
classes.definition: A rigid, reusable container used to hold and transport smaller items, per the customer's tote/bin class reference. Not a loose cardboard box.

images.caption: Blue rigid totes stacked on a blue pallet
IBC-style rigid container in a metal cage on a pallet

classes.name: Bin
classes.definition: A rigid, reusable storage container, distinct from Tote per the customer's class reference and distinct from Boxes (which are non-rigid/disposable).

images.caption: Three wheeled waste bins (glass, paper, plastic) in a row

classes.name: Rack
classes.definition: A multi-level storage structure that holds palletized or shelved goods. Annotate each rack section individually - never combine a full aisle into one cuboid.
cuboidRules: Never combine a full aisle into one cuboid

images.caption: Aisle of tall pallet racking with blue uprights and orange beams

classes.name: Shelf
classes.definition: An individual shelving unit or level used to store smaller, non-palletized items (distinct from a full Rack structure).

images.caption: Multi-level shelving unit with blue uprights and wooden shelf boards

classes.name: Conveyor
classes.definition: A belt, roller, or powered system used to move goods along a fixed path.

images.caption: Conveyor lines with totes and cartons, robot arms alongside

classes.name: Workstation
classes.definition: A fixed work area or setup (e.g. a packing or sorting station) where a task is performed.

images.caption: Workstation with benches, pegboard tool panels, monitor and cabinets

classes.name: Table
classes.definition: A general-purpose flat-surface furniture item, not part of a dedicated workstation.

images.caption: Flat-top work table with lower shelf in a warehouse

classes.name: Chair
classes.definition: A seating furniture item.

images.caption: Rolling stool with round green seat and footring
Four black stackable metal chairs

classes.name: Charging Station
classes.definition: Fixed equipment used to charge batteries for equipment such as forklifts, AGVs/AMRs, or other powered vehicles.

images.caption: Row of upright EV-style charging stations on wheeled bases in a clean facility

classes.name: Dock Door
classes.definition: A loading dock door or bay opening used for loading/unloading trailers.

images.caption: Row of numbered loading dock doors

classes.name: Safety Barrier
classes.definition: A physical barrier (railing, bollard, guard) installed to protect people, equipment, or defined zones.

images.caption: Yellow and black safety barrier railing and bollards along a walkway

classes.name: Machines
classes.definition: Industrial machinery in the scene that does not fit any other class.

images.caption: Stainless-steel industrial machine with control panel

classes.name: Boxes
classes.definition: A loose cardboard box or shipping carton (not a rigid reusable container). Cuboid includes any lid/flap overhang; annotate stacked-but-separable boxes individually, not as one stack cuboid.
cuboidRules: Annotate stacked-but-separable boxes individually, not as one stack cuboid

images.caption: Aisle between tall stacks of cardboard boxes

generalRules: Draw 3D bounding boxes (cuboids) around all objects from the label list, and assign the correct label.
Do not apply more than one cuboid to a single object.
Check every cuboid in every frame to ensure all LiDAR points are contained within the cuboid.
The cuboid center must be the geometric center of the entire object, including parts not currently visible.
Cuboid orientation: the length axis must align with the object's direction of travel; the height axis points upward; the width axis is perpendicular to both.
Object IDs must remain consistent across all frames in which the object appears. Do not switch IDs between objects.
IDs must be unsigned integers (e.g. 0, 1, 2). The order they are assigned is not important.
The cuboids should be properly aligned with the object in the 2D image. Please ensure the 3D cuboid fits the visible 2D object correctly.
Every visible object from the label list within a radius of 10m must be annotated in every frame where it appears.
Annotations must be complete, consistent, and tightly fitted to the object in every frame.

rules: Pre-labels are cuboids generated by a model to assist with the annotation process
Carefully review each pre-label and check whether it is relevant to the objects covered under your respective branch
If relevant: review the cuboid carefully, change its class to the appropriate ontology/class, and make sure it is properly aligned with the object across every frame
If not relevant: delete the pre-label and continue annotating the other relevant objects in the task
All pre-labels must be reviewed rather than accepted as-is
Cuboids should be properly aligned with the object in the 2D image
Ensure the 3D cuboid fits the visible 2D object correctly

referenceVideos.title: Stereo annotation for aligning with respect to the image

commonMistakes: Shrinking a Human cuboid to visible points instead of the full expected body volume
Using one cuboid for a whole rack aisle instead of one per rack section
Annotating stacked-but-separable boxes as a single stack cuboid
Annotating a wheelchair user only once (need both Wheelchair and Human with In-Wheelchair/ADA)
Accepting pre-labels as-is without reviewing class and alignment in every frame
Confusing Tote (rigid, reusable), Bin (rigid storage, distinct from Tote) and Boxes (non-rigid, disposable cardboard)
Labelling a Pallet Jack as Forklift (pallet jack is low, small, no raised mast)
Switching track IDs between objects, or reassigning an ID within a sequence
Placing the cuboid center on the visible points only instead of the geometric center of the entire object
Aligning the length axis arbitrarily instead of with the direction of travel
Leaving some LiDAR points of the object outside the cuboid in one or more frames
Skipping objects within 10 m, or putting two cuboids on one object
Cuboid not matching the object in the 2D camera image
Forgetting the occlusion or motion state on a cuboid

quizSeeds.prompt: An object is visible in 60% of its expected extent. Which occlusion state applies?
An object is only about 20% visible. Which occlusion state applies?
options: Partial, because the object is a Human

quizSeeds.prompt: Which ROI tier requires perfect quality with at most 5% error?
quizSeeds.explanation: ROI 0-5 needs perfect quality (5% error); 0-10 everything labelled; >10 m optional if LiDAR points are bad.

quizSeeds.prompt: Objects beyond 10 m must always be annotated even if the LiDAR points are poor.
quizSeeds.explanation: Beyond 10 m is good but optional if LiDAR points are bad.

quizSeeds.prompt: Which statement describes the required cuboid orientation?
options: Length axis along direction of travel, height up, width perpendicular to both
Length axis always along the sensor X axis
Height axis along direction of travel
Width axis along direction of travel
quizSeeds.explanation: Length aligns with direction of travel; height points upward; width is perpendicular to both.

quizSeeds.prompt: Which is a valid track ID rule?
options: IDs are unsigned integers and the assignment order does not matter
IDs must be assigned in order of distance from the sensor
IDs may be reused for a different object in a later frame
IDs are negative integers for static objects
quizSeeds.explanation: IDs are unsigned integers (0, 1, 2...), persistent across frames, never reassigned; order is not important.

quizSeeds.prompt: A track ID may be reassigned to a different object later in the same sequence.
quizSeeds.explanation: Never reassigned within a sequence/camera; do not switch IDs between objects.

quizSeeds.prompt: A model-generated pre-label cuboid is not relevant to the objects covered in your branch. What do you do?
options: Delete it and continue annotating the other relevant objects
quizSeeds.explanation: If not relevant, delete the pre-label. If relevant, review, set the class and align across every frame. Never accept as-is.

quizSeeds.prompt: If a pre-label looks roughly right, it can be accepted without review.
quizSeeds.explanation: All pre-labels must be reviewed rather than accepted as-is.

quizSeeds.prompt: A person is seated in a wheelchair. What do you annotate?
options: Only the Human with activity In-Wheelchair/ADA
Both a Wheelchair cuboid and a Human cuboid with activity In-Wheelchair/ADA
quizSeeds.explanation: Annotate the device as Wheelchair and also the person as Human with In-Wheelchair/ADA.

quizSeeds.prompt: A long aisle of racking is visible. How should it be annotated?
options: One cuboid covering the full aisle
quizSeeds.explanation: Annotate each rack section individually - never combine a full aisle into one cuboid.

quizSeeds.prompt: Which class is shown: loose cardboard cartons stacked in an aisle?
quizSeeds.explanation: Boxes are loose cardboard boxes/shipping cartons (non-rigid, disposable). Tote and Bin are rigid reusable containers. Stacked-but-separable boxes are annotated individually.

quizSeeds.prompt: Which class is shown: rigid reusable blue containers stacked on a pallet?
quizSeeds.explanation: Totes are rigid, reusable containers for smaller items; not loose cardboard boxes.

quizSeeds.prompt: Which class is shown: a low machine with two forks and a handle, no raised mast?
quizSeeds.explanation: A Pallet Jack is low and small with two forks and no raised mast; a Forklift has a fork/mast assembly and operator compartment.

quizSeeds.prompt: A Human is half hidden behind a rack. How should the cuboid be drawn?
options: Estimate the hidden body portion and keep a physically representative full-body cuboid
Skip annotation until the person is fully visible
Use two cuboids, visible and hidden parts
quizSeeds.explanation: Cuboids shall not be reduced solely to fit visible pixels; estimate the hidden portion. Only one cuboid per object.
